name: BATON claim-corruption benchmark v1
description: Labelled claim-corruption instances harvested from real AI-agent output written before BATON existed. Ground truth for every quantitative row was independently recomputed from primary data (D:\Projects\Stark-Core\state\dispatches.jsonl), never carried forward from a summary.

corpus.note: All three documents predate BATON. None was written with a checker in mind. The corruption in them is organic.

ground_truth_recompute.method: deduplicate on `key`, last-write-wins; status=='completed' counts as a completion
ground_truth_recompute.guards_present_false: 313 of 315 (2 records carry no `guards` field at all)
ground_truth_recompute.WARNING: This block is itself perishable and that is the point. The distinct-dispatch count read 309 in LOKI-ATTACK.md (2026-08-29, earlier), 311 on the first recompute of this session, and 313 twenty minutes later in the same session. The file is appended to live. Re-run `node bench/recompute.js` before quoting any figure here; do not cite this block from memory. BATON cannot detect that this block has gone stale - that is limitation 2 in PROJECT-REFERENCE.md section 7, demonstrated on the benchmark's own metadata.

scope_classes.handoff_integrity: Origin and restatement both exist in the corpus. BATON is designed to have an opinion. THESE ARE THE SCORED ROWS - precision, recall and false-positive rate are computed over this class only.
scope_classes.origin_truth: The figure was already wrong when first written; the restatement copied it faithfully. BATON is designed to be SILENT here (trust boundary). Scored separately as 'correctly silent'. A REJECT on one of these rows would be a false positive against the trust boundary's own promise.
scope_classes.invention: A downstream claim with no origin anywhere in the corpus. Default gate() emits no verdict (the `unaligned` honesty receipt). Reported separately - this is the measured size of the coverage gap named in LOKI-ATTACK.md finding 2.
scope_classes.hard_case: Genuinely ambiguous at the level of a non-semantic checker. Excluded from the headline metric and reported on its own line, with the reasoning stated. Hiding these would make the benchmark dishonest.

instance_count_note: LOKI-ATTACK.md and the pitch cite 'eight more instances'. That count comes from loki-deep-trust.md:295-302, which enumerates three named figures plus 'every per-agent figure in raven's line 19 - five instances', and friday's 2/37 appears in both halves. The distinct, individually-checkable pairs are enumerated below as B01-B12. Cite the enumeration, not the headline number, if a judge counts.

origin.focus: 2 of 252 dispatch records carry a confidence value (0.79%)

restatement.text: The literature measures instruction-following decay from ~100% down to 50-91% under load, stacking, or distance. Kevin's fleet reports 0.79%. That is not the same regime - it is roughly two orders of magnitude below the worst published degradation.

instances.how_ground_truth_established: Direct read of both lines in the same file. The corruption is structural, not numeric: the rate survives, the denominator that made it meaningful does not, and the bare rate is then compared against a published range whose base is different.
instances.why_it_matters: Same agent, same file, 15 lines apart. No handoff involved. This is the demo.
instances.notes: Both lines are in ONE document by ONE agent. Do not describe this as a chain or a hop.

A checker that fires here is punishing honest paraphrase. LOKI-ATTACK.md finding 4 is that nobody had measured how often BATON says no to something that was fine. This row, and B04, are how that gets measured.

instances.why_it_matters: THE VOLUNTEERED COUNTEREXAMPLE. BATON returns ACCEPT and the number is wrong by a factor of ~3. It was wrong at origin and copied perfectly - clean transit, poisoned source. The mentor's threat-model review (BATON_Threat_Model_and_Security_Architecture.md:187-206) uses these exact two numbers as its own textbook example of 'Threat 1 - Origin Poisoning'.
instances.notes: NEVER present this as something BATON catches. Present it as the honesty beat. Note also that its true value has moved twice - which makes it simultaneously the best illustration of the evidence-staleness limitation.

instances.how_ground_truth_established: Direct read. The figure is restated in heavily rewritten prose - a table cell becomes a rhetorical question, 'completion' becomes 'finished jobs', the agent's name is dropped for 'this worker' - and the numerator, denominator and meaning all survive intact.
instances.why_it_matters: THE PARAPHRASE-ROBUSTNESS TEST, and the second false-positive probe. This is exactly the transformation BATON claims to survive: no ID carried, wording entirely different, quantity preserved. If BATON fires here it is broken in the way that matters most, because heavy paraphrase is the normal case, not the corrupt one.

instances.true_value: the same numerator (2) is quoted against two different bases - 378 and 252 - 61 lines apart in ONE document. 2/378 = 0.53%, 2/252 = 0.79%.
instances.how_ground_truth_established: Direct read of both lines in the same file. No external data needed: the document contradicts itself.
instances.why_it_matters: An intra-document base contradiction. Note also that line 20 carries an explicit caveat - 'a floor, not a measurement' - which line 81 drops while promoting the figure to a headline. That makes this a caveat_loss candidate as well as a base contradiction; either verdict is a correct catch.
instances.notes: This row is why the corpus is interesting: the SAME AGENT flagged its own figure as unreliable and then used it as a headline 61 lines later.

restatement.text: I measured a second, harder one this run: guards.present false on 378 of 378 = 0.00%, at a larger denominator.

instances.true_value: semantically consistent with the origin; numerically its complement
instances.how_ground_truth_established: Direct read. The origin states '378/378 = 100%' meaning 100% of dispatches have guards.present == false. The restatement states the same fact as '378 of 378 = 0.00%', meaning 0% compliance. Same base, same subject, inverted rate.
instances.why_it_matters: HONEST HARD CASE, and it is here precisely because it is inconvenient. A non-semantic checker sees 100% -> 0.00% on the same base and the same unit and fires value_drift. That is defensible (the surface claim genuinely inverted, and a reader skimming would be misled) and it is also arguably a false positive (the author is stating the complement, not corrupting the figure). BATON has no polarity model and cannot tell these apart. Excluded from the headline precision/recall figure and reported on its own line. A benchmark that quietly dropped this row to make its numbers look better would be committing the exact sin this project exists to catch.

restatement.text: We ran an 18-agent fleet for six months. We had a fleet-wide reporting policy. Our own telemetry observed it twice in 378 dispatches, and a separate safety guard zero times in 378.

instances.why_it_matters: THE COVERAGE-GAP MEASUREMENT. There is no origin claim for 'six months' anywhere in the corpus - the number was invented at the point of writing. Under default gate() this produces NO VERDICT: it lands in the `unaligned` honesty receipt and the pipeline proceeds. That is LOKI-ATTACK.md finding 2, made concrete and countable rather than argued. Under `strict` it becomes REJECT - no_origin.

It appears eleven times in that file and in nine other files in the corpus. It is the single most damaging error in the corpus and the default gate does not stop it.

annotation_note: Each origin/restatement carries a `focus`: the minimal claim-bearing clause, taken verbatim from the cited line. This is claim-level annotation, the same granularity the summarization-faithfulness literature evaluates at, and it is necessary because a real corpus line often carries several unrelated quantities. `bench/run.js` uses `focus` when present and falls back to the full line otherwise. Running with --raw disables focus entirely and measures the harder, more realistic document-granularity task - see bench/README.md, which reports both numbers because the gap between them is itself a finding.
